[p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! Teamfight Manager 2 will be sharing consistent development updates every 2–3 weeks through development logs. We appreciate your interest and support. [/p][p][/p][h2]Preparing the Demo Build[/h2][p]Following up on our previous dev log, we’ve continued making improvements and working on the UI in preparation for the demo build.[/p][p] [/p][h3]New Game UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/2f8892cd310d9f6931560bd20e35b066cc29a240.png"][/img][/p][p]When starting a new game, you can select the team you want to play and configure various options.[/p][p][/p][h3]Schedule UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e83b5f5d025106ec57ec8ae16b978d03e8a8a5ac.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/7c6d725d26815c41994ad64581f223ff34ba893c.png"][/img][/p][p]This UI allows you to check the detailed schedule. You can view it in a calendar format or browse the full list of events.[/p][p][/p][h3]Home UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/f6ba0ca5d4b8be4402537412426d23b93014154e.png"][/img][/p][p]This screen provides a summary of your team’s current status at a glance.[/p][p][/p][h3]Statistics UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/b042cc7aee12de9d61939eacb111912876b11b31.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/afd10cc03c37a6cdedfecb5508e81989e76c1b20.png"][/img][/p][p]You can check various statistics for each player and champion.[/p][p]
[/p][h3]In-Game Health Gauge[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/9e104e5121c9b08aafd18b6d65487d98c48ced70.png"][/img][/p][p]To improve visibility during complex battle situations, we’ve updated the design of the in-game health gauge.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, we’re continuing optimization work and improving the coach training process to prepare for the demo build. We look forward to sharing the demo during the Steam Next Fest, taking place from October 13 to October 20![/p][p]
[/p][p]That’s all for this dev log. Thank you for reading![/p]

notes.title: Devlog #13
notes.content: [p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! Teamfight Manager 2 will be sharing consistent development updates every 2–3 weeks through development logs. We appreciate your interest and support.[/p][p][/p][h2]UI Changes & Improvements[/h2][p]We’ve been continuously adding, improving, and updating the internal UI.[/p][p][/p][h3]Match UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/6640912855815d6c6b28087c3dc83a8917631520.png"][/img][/p][p]The match screen layout has been updated. Previously, the match display was centered with related information on both sides. Now, the match screen is placed on the left, and all match-related information is gathered on the right.[/p][p]While the shifted match screen may feel a bit unusual at first, we believe this new layout better captures the feeling of a head coach watching and analyzing the match with access to various data in real time.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/ff236ed30584b902d28f528201df096bf9bf337d.png"][/img][/p][p]By clicking the "View Details" button during a match, you can check more detailed information related to the game. [/p][h3]Match Result UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e6c9f68214c63e0dbf1aa5c37f88c562d39a86d7.png"][/img][/p][p]We’ve added a new system to calculate player ratings for each match, along with an MVP feature that awards the title to the best-performing player.[/p][p][/p][h3]Loading UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/5a1f8f8104173af514a5c773e964f72d15db6bc8.png"][/img][/p][p]A new loading screen UI has been added for transitions from the management screen.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Champion Info UI[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/20103f143a30976db0777b923c28ba4a8c94df2a.png"][/img][/p][p]A new UI has been added to check detailed champion information.[/p][p][/p][h2]Match Engine[/h2][p]In the upcoming demo build, our goal is to let players experience the core content of the game by progressing through the Coach Training mode, playing matches from 2v2 up to 5v5.[/p][p]Originally, we aimed to include recruitment, transfers, and scouting in the demo’s Coach Training process. However, we decided it would be difficult to fully implement transfers as meaningful content by the demo’s release. Therefore, management systems—including recruitment—will be prepared for Early Access, while the demo will focus on the core gameplay elements such as the match engine, ban-pick phase, and strategies.[/p][p]During this process, significant changes have been made to both player stats and strategies.[/p][p][/p][h3]Player Stats[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/a92cd4c7416b1cfac58129878d286f11bfa934f4.png"][/img][/p][p]Here’s the new detailed player stats screen. Previously, stats were limited to four categories—Mechanics, Judgment, Mental, and Focus—but during test play, we found this too limited to make team building interesting. We decided to break stats down into more specific categories so that coaches can consider a wider variety of roster compositions.[/p][p]The new stats are divided into two types: beneficial stats (higher is better) and personality traits that shape a player’s style.[/p][p][/p][p]Beneficial Stats[/p][list][*][p]Last Hit – Ability to land the final blow on minions, neutral monsters, and epic monsters.[/p][/*][*][p]Skill Dodge – Ability to evade enemy skillshots.[/p][/*][*][p]Skill Accuracy – Ability to land skillshots on enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Control Speed – Shortens the delay between inputs; essentially, the player’s ability to execute commands quickly.[/p][/*][*][p]Positioning – Ability to position advantageously by weighing risks and rewards.[/p][/*][*][p]Prediction – Ability to anticipate unseen enemy positions.[/p][/*][*][p]Awareness – Ability to process complex situations without missing any key enemy or ally actions, especially in chaotic fights.[/p][/*][*][p]Focus – Ability to maintain performance in late-game situations.[/p][/*][*][p]Mental – Ability to maintain performance when the game is going badly.[/p][/*][*][p]Judgment – Ability to make accurate calls about advantage and disadvantage.[/p][/*][/list][p]Personality Traits[/p][list][*][p]Shotcalling – Frequency of giving orders and communicating game flow to teammates.[/p][/*][*][p]Roaming – Tendency to move to other lanes or jungle to assist.[/p][/*][*][p]Aggression – Willingness to take high-risk actions.[/p][/*][*][p]Ego – Tendency to play in a self-centered way.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]While stat names and compositions may still change during development, our current goal is to have around 10–15 specialized stats that affect specific in-game situations. Although this adds complexity, we believe it will allow for deeper, more strategic gameplay.[/p][p] [/p][h3]Strategies[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/f98107392073d3c90224e4a5eaca2b37c5d15857.png"][/img][/p][p]Strategies have also seen major updates alongside stats. For example, early-game strategies now allow you to choose whether to heavily pressure a specific lane or invade the enemy jungle. In the mid to late game, you can decide whether to split push or focus on teamfights versus macro play.[/p][p]We’ve also added personal tactics for assigning roles in teamfights, letting battles unfold according to the coach’s vision. Current teamfight roles include Initiator, Assassin, Frontline, Midline, and Backline. The same champion will behave differently depending on the assigned role.[/p][p]For example, assigning a fighter champion as an Initiator will have them focus on positioning and skill use to start favorable fights, whereas assigning them to the Backline will make them protect allies from incoming threats.[/p][p][/p][h2]Other Changes[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/c1cda0e48b85c9a6ad0ad0a4f0811781b001b346.gif"][/img][/p][p]We’ve added new kill streak effects when taking down multiple enemies in quick succession, and gold gains are now displayed when earned. We continue to make small but impactful improvements across various areas.[/p][p][/p][h2]Demo[/h2][p]The demo will be available during Steam Next Fest from October 13 to 20. We look forward to your interest and feedback![/p][p][/p][p]That's all for this development log. Thank you very much for reading![/p]

notes.title: Devlog #12
notes.content: [p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! Teamfight Manager 2 will be sharing consistent development updates every 2–3 weeks through development logs. We appreciate your interest and support.[/p][p][/p][h2]Coach Training[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/1e71eacfb1789711430b94c3cc248736376f6a16.png"][/img][/p][p]The tutorial process in Teamfight Manager 2 takes place through a course called “Coach Training.” When you first start the game, you can choose whether or not to take the Coach Training. If you decide to take it, you will be able to learn the game’s systems step by step, starting from the most basic elements.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/d80d9f3e2be2ea8a0dcd3d19cffd57aa1e86a766.png"][/img][/p][p]The Coach Training process is similar to the previous title, where you started with 2v2 matches and gradually expanded the rules through the season until you became accustomed to the game. In this process, you will sequentially learn the game from 2v2 all the way to 5v5 matches.[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]2v2 match: Each team selects only the Bottom and Support positions, and the game is played solely on the bottom lane.[/p][/*][*][p]3v3 match: Teams select Mid, Bottom, and Support positions, and lane battles take place in both the mid and bottom lanes.[/p][/*][*][p]4v4 match: Except for the Jungle, only Top, Mid, and Bottom lane battles are played.[/p][/*][*][p]5v5 match: The Jungle is added, and the match is played under the same rules as a standard game.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]As shown above, the complexity of matches is expanded step by step so that players can learn the full game rules. Additionally, in 2v2 to 4v4 matches, the twin towers protecting the sanctuary are removed for faster gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e0ae4d1eecf7f16900f50acb74b2ca4107753bba.png"][/img][/p][p]By gradually expanding the rules from 2v2 to 5v5, players will not only get used to drafting and Champions, but will also learn team management features one at a time. The goal is to ensure that even players unfamiliar with the MOBA genre will feel comfortable with the game by the time they complete the Coach Training process.[/p][p][/p][h2]Improvements[/h2][p]Alongside this, we are also continuing work on adding and improving various UI elements for the demo build, balancing Champions, and applying background music and sound effects.[/p][p][/p][p]That's all for this development log. Thank you very much for reading![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Devlog #10
notes.content: [p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! Teamfight Manager 2 will be sharing consistent development updates every 2–3 weeks through development logs. We appreciate your interest and support. [/p][p][/p][h2] New Champion Added, AI Improvements [/h2][p][url="https://www.youtube.com/watch/QCtlTh13-ik"]https://www.youtube.com/watch/QCtlTh13-ik[/url][/p][p][url="https://www.youtube.com/watch/6w5DCRbOPeI"]https://www.youtube.com/watch/6w5DCRbOPeI[/url][/p][p]We were a bit hesitant to reveal full match simulations, given that the match engine is still lacking in many areas. However, we felt it would be better to transparently share our progress and show how we improve going forward, so we decided to release full match videos. [/p][p] [/p][p]Let’s briefly touch on the technical side. The match engine in Teamfight Manager 2 has three core development goals: [/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Speed: Simulations need to run as quickly as possible. As mentioned in a previous devlog, Teamfight Manager 2 requires frequent match simulations for many different purposes. If simulations are slow, it results in long wait times during gameplay. [/p][/*][*][p]Scalability: The match engine’s structure must allow for easy AI updates and modifications. This is critical for productivity, especially given our small development team, and it also helps prepare for future mod support. [/p][/*][*][p]Performance: Matches should be enjoyable and immersive to watch, and the players should feel like they’re performing at a high level. [/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]It’s nearly impossible to fully satisfy all three goals at once. There are clear trade-offs—enhancing performance often comes at the cost of speed and scalability. And with many other parts of the game needing development, we have limited time to spend exclusively on the match engine. So, we’ve taken an approach that builds a scalable and reasonably fast engine structure, then works to maximize performance within those constraints. [/p][p] [/p][p]Through multiple rounds of testing and redesigns, we’ve finally established a scalable structure that allows for incremental improvements to the match engine. [/p][p] [/p][p]Here’s a simple breakdown of how the player AI framework currently works: each player’s behavior is divided into three stages—Tactical Decision, Micro Decision, and Actual Execution. [/p][p] [/p][list][*][p]Tactical Decision: High-level decisions about what the player believes they should be doing strategically—such as pushing the bottom lane, preparing for the Morgard objective, or attempting a gank. [/p][/*][*][p]Micro Decision: Based on the tactical decision, this determines what the player should do in the short term—like chasing a nearby enemy, backing off slightly, attacking, or dodging. [/p][/*][*][p]Actual Execution: Inputs that carry out the micro decision—such as issuing a move command to specific coordinates or using a skill to close distance quickly. [/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][p]To simplify: each player evaluates potential tactical decisions by calculating a score for how beneficial they’d be in the current situation, and selects the one with the highest score. Then, they generate micro decision candidates to carry out the chosen tactic, evaluate their scores, and perform the most optimal one. [/p][p] [/p][p]This structure makes it relatively easy to add and refine new behaviors. For example, if we want players to invade the enemy jungle as a group early in the game, we can add that behavior as a separate tactical decision and assign an appropriate score—allowing it to be adopted without major structural changes. [/p][p] [/p][p]At this stage, we’ve established the match engine’s core framework and implemented the fundamental behaviors. Some aspects, like late-game operations or teamfights, are still lacking and can lead to awkward behavior—but these are exactly the parts we plan to focus on next, to enhance the overall AI. [/p][p] [/p][p]That’s it for this development log. Thanks for reading this long post! [/p]

notes.title: Devlog #9
notes.content: [p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! We plan to share steady development updates for Teamfight Manager 2 every 2–3 weeks, so please stay tuned. [/p][p][/p][h2]Items[/h2][p]In Devlog #7 we briefly mentioned that the rule overhaul would introduce gold and items. In this log we will explain the new item system in more detail.[/p][p][/p][p]In Teamfight Manager 2 each champion can purchase up to three items. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/ba990051fb9d353b9101df59e5d238d7e395d7f8.png"][/img][/p][p]The first things you can buy are the six Tier-1 items shown above. Each one boosts a single stat: Attack Damage, Attack Speed, Armor, Magic Resistance, Ability Power, or Health. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/9aa310da6a61f5d20896698ad4c9a0b67b35c602.png"][/img][/p][p]A Tier-1 item can be upgraded to Tier-2 for an additional amount of gold. Doing so keeps the original stat bonus and adds an extra effect. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e7f06fbc2a22090349fe926898c20b83bfd8d6e3.png"][/img][/p][p]You can then pay more gold to upgrade from Tier-2 to Tier-3. There are no recipes: every Tier-1 branches into four predetermined Tier-2 items, and every Tier-2 branches into three predetermined Tier-3 items. Because the game needs to stay readable—both for players and for the AI—we chose a simple, linear upgrade path.[/p][p] [/p][p]Every Tier-1 item therefore leads to four Tier-2 items, and each Tier-2 leads to three Tier-3 items. Since the same Tier-3 can be reached from two different Tier-2 paths, each stat line ends up with six unique Tier-3 items. In total there are 66 items: 6 Tier-1, 24 Tier-2, and 36 Tier-3.[/p][p] [/p][p]Because two different Tier-2 items can upgrade into the same Tier-3, you can tailor your path even if your final destination is identical. For example, upgrading the Tier-1 Iron Blade into Piercing Blade grants armor penetration, whereas upgrading it into Lifeleech Blade  grants lifesteal. Both can later be upgraded into Bloodreaver, which combines both effects and adds a unique passive. If you need sustain first, build Lifeleech Blade; if you need armor penetration first, build Piercing Blade—even though you’ll end up with the same Tier-3 item. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/8298296614cb27ed605b29f3df088494ca2ec1fd.png"][/img][/p][p]Here are all current item icons: 6 Tier-1, 24 Tier-2, and 36 Tier-3. Not every passive is implemented yet, but the stats and upgrade logic are already in place. [/p][p][/p][h3]Choosing Item Builds[/h3][p]At the moment champions purchase and upgrade items automatically according to the AI’s judgement. Our intention is to keep that convenience while still letting coaches steer build direction at a high level. If a coach had to hand-pick every single item every game it would be overwhelming, but having zero influence can feel frustrating—so we’re experimenting with lightweight ways to nudge the AI without micromanagement. We’ll share details in a future log.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Adding New Champions [/h2][p]Teamfight Manager 2 will launch in Early Access with 60 champions: the 40 originals plus 20 brand-new ones. Concepts and designs are finalized, and roughly half of the implementations are done.[/p][p][/p][p]Below are a few in-game shots of some new champions.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/60656bd84c817a6b39ff0bc8379b2c27623f18d4.gif"][/img][/p][p]Gameplay footage of the new Hammerman champion.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/86bc485c9d73e39d76f7f894b2fbde00b7e78be1.gif"][/img][/p][p]Gameplay footage of the new Staff Master champion.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/fa5cd985c6cdc0b2826a53d6ec75833f357f1bf2.gif"][/img][/p][p]Gameplay footage of the new Cavalryman champion. [/p][p][/p][h3]AI Improvements[/h3][p]While adding new champions, we’re also re-working the AI so it can make proper use of each champion’s mechanics, and we’re steadily upgrading overall play quality. [/p][p][/p][p]A quick explanation of the workflow: simply staring at match replays has its limits—it’s slow and it’s hard to judge whether a tweak truly helped. Instead, as mentioned in earlier devlogs, we rely on data. We have a tool that can run huge batches of simulations and export detailed statistics, so every AI pass starts with this tool.[/p][p][/p][p]Because the simulation architecture separates “player AI” from the core game loop, we can load multiple AIs at once. For each test we lock one team to the previous (“old”) AI and let the other team use the new AI. If the new version wins more often, we regard it as smarter than the old one.[/p][p] [/p][p]We also harvest extra metrics—e.g., average gold difference at the 3-minute mark—to see whether the new AI actually laned better. We check how often the team that secures the first Morguard ends up winning, and so on, to make sure the overall balance still makes sense. [/p][p][/p][p]Of course, better numbers don’t automatically mean better spectacle. So after confirming the stats we still watch real matches to verify that the play looks better, not just scores better.[/p][p][/p][p]The “baseline” AI we froze during the last devlog handled only the basics of 5-v-5 play. The current WIP version beats that baseline about 66 % of the time and finishes games more than a minute faster (weak AIs tend to stall instead of closing).[/p][p][/p][p]Our goal is to iterate like this—each new AI aiming for roughly a 60–70 % win rate over the previous one—until the simulation feels convincingly solid. That said, plenty of silly plays remain, and we still don’t see as much tactical variety as we want. We’ll keep pushing so that the Early-Access build ships with the strongest AI we can manage.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s it for this devlog. Thanks for reading this long post![/p]

notes.title: Devlog #8
notes.content: [p]Hello, this is Team Samoyed! We aim to consistently share the development progress of Teamfight Manager 2 through devlogs every 2 to 3 weeks. We appreciate your continued interest and support.[/p][p][/p][h2]UI Update Work[/h2][p]We’ve updated the UI for draft picks, tactics, and more to match the new 5v5 rule set and adjusted game systems to allow for proper gameplay under these new rules.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/83b54af28940167b2094d05d724db9ae3f7fc291.png"][/img][/p][p]This is the new draft pick screen UI. In addition to UI changes for the 5v5 format, we’re also working on a full redesign of the game’s UI aesthetics.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/d8a4202c5b111a37d4d8caf0be7e5fbdd25809f8.png"][/img][/p][p]This is the updated tactics settings UI. A new tactic for responding to Morgard has been added. Along with this, we’d like to talk briefly about our intended direction for the AI in the game simulation.[/p][p][/p][p]The AI we are aiming for in Teamfight Manager 2 is not designed to be smart or perfect. In a simulation that must run very quickly, that’s not realistic—and more importantly, what we’re really aiming for is an AI that visibly reflects your draft and tactical instructions and makes the game enjoyable to watch.[/p][p][/p][p]Teamfight Manager 2 is a game played from the perspective of a coach. What matters is not whether the AI performs perfectly in-game, but whether the player can feel that their intended strategy and picks are being realized during the match.[/p][p][/p][p]The current tactics system and match flow are based on this idea. Right now, the flow of a match is structured as follows:[/p][list][*][p]First 3 minutes: The laning phase. Each player stays in their lane and plays out the early game.[/p][/*][*][p]After 3 minutes: One minute before Morgard spawns, the operations phase begins. Players will reposition according to the “Morgard tactics formation.” Depending on whether you select Group Together / 1-4 Split / 1-3-1 Split formations, players are distributed accordingly.[/p][/*][*][p]When Morgard spawns, the team will attempt to slay it depending on lane states and advantage level. The “Hunt Attempt” and “Combat During Hunt” tactics settings determine whether the team focuses on hunting Morgard or on engaging the enemy.[/p][/*][*][p]This pattern continues and repeats with each Morgard spawn after the 3-minute mark.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Since this high-level structure of the match is consistent, viewers can more easily identify key moments. During the first 3 minutes, the focus is on how well your team wins or loses the laning phase. After the 3-minute mark, attention shifts to whether the game flows according to your chosen tactics for the operations phase.[/p][p][/p][p]For example, let’s say you selected a 1-4 formation, passive hunting behavior for Morgard, and aggressive combat behavior during the hunt. You also drafted a top lane champion who excels at laning and 1v1s. The rest of your team consists of champions suited for skirmishing and pokings. If your top laner dominates the lane early, they can then pressure the bottom lane during the operations phase, forcing the enemy to defend, while your other four players create standoff pressure around Morgard and seek advantages through small fights.[/p][p][/p][p]As a coach, you consider these tactics while watching the match. Because the flow is always consistent and progresses according to your tactics, you can clearly identify what went wrong when things don’t go your way. Maybe your side lane pressure didn’t work out because you failed to build enough of a lead early on. Or maybe the opponent used a Group Together formation with a strong initiating comp and punished your 4-man standoff with a full 5v4 engage. There are countless possible outcomes. And each leads you to reconsider what the best tactic, draft, or team composition would be.[/p][p][/p][p]This is the kind of game flow we’re aiming for in Teamfight Manager 2. Of course, the AI isn’t yet executing all of this perfectly, and there’s still a lot of work ahead.[/p][p][/p][h3]AI Improvements[/h3][p]That was a long explanation about AI direction—but rather than just talk in theory, we’d like to follow up on our last devlog by showing some of the improvements we’ve made.[/p][p][/p][p]Previously, standoffs and fights around Morgard felt stiff and awkward. We’ve updated the AI to make these encounters look and feel more natural.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e9d7f3990808caed98522c86403860df53bc3678.gif"][/img][/p][p]Blue team is nearly done slaying Morgard. Red team realizes this and rushes to contest. The Fighter is trying to block their approach.[/p][p][/p][p]However, the Clown on Red joins the fight, helps take out the Fighter, and in the retreat phase, Blue’s formation gets split on both sides.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/e01896eb2dda344e8b850d0fd5e42bb43292bc00.gif"][/img][/p][p]Next, the Lancer dives Blue’s Swordsman and Archer on the left, while the Clown focuses the Ice Mage on the right. The Dancer and Knight are too far back to follow up, and the Lancer gets killed by the Swordsman and Archer.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/1ee4537c72e938c886a43078f4bdded0f7c4c9ec.gif"][/img][/p][p]However, in the next phase of the fight, the Knight lands a strong taunt, and the Dancer and Clown follow up to eliminate the Swordsman and Archer.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/8d6a23670689d016956120424dc6a3c56a52f917.gif"][/img][/p][p]The Dancer, low on HP, retreats and narrowly finishes a trade with the Clown. But as development has progressed, we reached a point where switching to a more capable backend was necessary—so we’ve now completed that transition.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/7473d4acc6dbd3208c46c31ff49e88e9ebec3c10.png"][/img][/p][p]On the left is the rendering with the old engine backend; on the right is the rendering with the new backend. notes.title: Devlog #7
notes.content:
Hello, this is Team Samoyed! We plan to share the development progress of Teamfight Manager 2 consistently through devlogs every 2 to 3 weeks. We hope for your continued interest and support.

In this edition, we’ll be discussing changes to in-game match rules.

[h2]Map and Rule Changes[/h2]

Previously, Teamfight Manager 2 was being developed based on a 4v4 format with 2 lanes. The main reason for this decision was the direction that the in-game simulation should remain as simple and easy to understand as possible.

As mentioned several times in previous devlogs, the concept of a game within a game is difficult to handle in many ways. Since it’s not a real existing game, if the rules are too complex or hard to grasp, the barrier to entry becomes too high. That's why we wanted to keep the game as simple as possible.

In line with this intent, we aimed to structure the game screen so that the entire battlefield could be seen at a glance. However, to fit a 5v5 format with 3 lanes into a single screen, there were spatial limitations. If we tried to display all 5v5 gameplay on one screen, the champion sizes would become too small to observe any detailed action.

Thus, at the early stage of development, we decided to simplify the rules as much as possible and display the full map on a single screen. We excluded familiar MOBA concepts like gold, items, and epic monsters, and built the game based on the simplest possible rule set.

However, these initial decisions weren’t all necessarily correct. Throughout development, we encountered various issues derived from these choices — and conversely, some things we expected to be problems turned out not to be.

[olist]
[*] Camera Issue: Initially, we thought showing the full game screen would make the match easier to understand. But after implementing features like feedback and the zoomable observing camera, we found that viewing a zoomed-in camera focused on key moments actually made the game much easier to follow. Instead of manually tracking all the action across the screen, it was better to algorithmically detect major moments and highlight them through the camera. Also, since most MOBA games adopt a 5v5, 3-lane structure, players found it easier to understand the game flow even with small rule differences, compared to the unfamiliar 4v4, 2-lane setup.

[*] Supporter Positioning Problem: We tried to differentiate the game by removing gold and items, but had trouble clearly distinguishing between the support and bottom roles. In a system where level differences come only from experience, we found it hard to make the stat differences between supporters and bottom laners function meaningfully as intended.

[*] Simplified Match Flow: Since there were no rewards for gaining lane priority or pushing lanes, the flow of the game became overly simplified, and average match times grew too long. Especially, even minor changes to tower stats (attack power and HP) caused large fluctuations in match duration. We realized it was necessary to improve gameplay when a team had gained control through lane pushing.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/a09b64d16fa0a4b9e5b6eb97b158fa7e08ac6400.png[/img]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/2e0060495e55aa5c151fd9b7d18077e551370e89.png[/img]

Based on these considerations, we transitioned the system to a 5v5, 3-lane format. The images above show the current in-development build.

The details of the rule changes compared to the previous version are as follows:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/89c5906197e307fc73c3f4af4c3e696b7d68dfc6.png[/img]

The map has been changed to a 5v5, 3-lane layout, and a mid lane position has been added. In addition to the first tower on each lane, two towers defending the relic have been added. Previously, the relic also functioned as an attacking tower, but it is now a non-attacking object.

Gold and item systems have been introduced. Alongside this, new stats such as Ability Power and Magic Resistance have been added to champions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/3a7215f099e347c5c4da1070f87e78ba93a47e7a.gif[/img]

The epic monster “Morgard” has been added. Morgard spawns at the 4-minute mark in-game and respawns every 2 minutes and 30 seconds (subject to change). When slain, Morgard grants the slaying team’s champions permanent stat boosts, and also provides a 1-minute buff that empowers nearby minions.

These changes have undeniably made the rules more complex than before, but they also solve many of the gameplay issues we previously faced. We believe the added complexity is well worth the improvements. Of course, we also plan to invest more effort into tutorials to explain these new rules effectively.

Below are several gameplay scenes:

[h3]Early Game Scenarios[/h3]

[img]https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/14765581062017826069/231E7ACE9BEF048FB9D32383560D701FFB41CAED/?imw=1024&imh=1024&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=true[/img]  
A clash occurred between junglers near the top lane. It was about to end with Garvey being taken down one-sidedly, but top laner owo joined the fight, ending it as a 1-for-1 trade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/be144a8629bdec070f95553552f2cbb1ae16c454.gif[/img]  
A grab in bottom lane leads to a quick kill right after engaging.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/047859859f7dbd969fb67231c502b5c9386a9299.gif[/img]  
Red team’s jungle Wink ambushes in a bush and initiates on Blue jungle RavWar. Although the situation was dangerous, Blue’s top Pyosik lands a skill on Red top Skin and, with proper focus, takes down Skin — resulting in a 1-for-1 trade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/d0b74c9e719c3c0621d350d84f4390a14f2f3906.gif[/img]  
A gunner dodges all of the executioner’s skills during the midlane laning phase and gains an early advantage with effective kiting.

[h3]Mid-to-Late Game: Epic Monster Hunt[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/c8f871b94e3ad7f6cc0abe0aff54af4ab5a5c4e5.gif[/img]  
The red team attempts a sneaky Morgard kill but gets spotted and backs off.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45467379/51c8c8128ea5409ad64c08f470288222e26c2c95.gif[/img]  
Red team dives in with their ogre and monk frontliners, but a skill combo from Blue wipes out the ogre and swordman in an instant, leading to a crushing defeat.

These rule changes have allowed for much more strategic depth and variation in team compositions. However, with increased complexity, AI decision-making now also needs to be more sophisticated — and there's still a lot of room for improvement.

Tasks like building item strategies, redefining champion roles and skills for the new system, and adjusting tactics for epic monsters all remain.

Since rule changes of this scale are such massive undertakings, there are still many unpolished areas. Nonetheless, we firmly believe that these new rules are more fun and better suited to the game than the old ones. We’ll address the remaining issues step-by-step and cover those updates in future devlogs.

That’s it for this devlog. Thanks for reading!
